sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent persons and have been falsely implicated in the present case due to rivalry.
He further submits that the opposite party No.2 has initiated two proceedings against the applicants for the same cause of action.

Earlier also the opposite party No.2 implicated the applicant No.1, namely-Vijay Bahadur Singh aggrieved by that,
the applicant No.1 approached this Court by filing an Application U/S 482 No.101 of 2023 and the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 09.01.2023 passed the following order:-
"Heard learned counsel for applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

By means of this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicant has sought following relief:-
"Wherefore, it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to set aside summoning order dated 28.07.2022 passed by learned Additional Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 3, District Unnao in Criminal Trial No.
1983 of 2022 arising out of Complaint Case No. 175 of 2020 (CNR No.
UPUN04-000175-2020)."

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 3, District Unnao
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that the applicant has falsely been implicated in this case.

Further submission is that the trial court passed the summoning order dated 28.07.2022 without examining any witnesses and without recorded statement under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and 202 Cr.P.C., which is mandatory as per law.

It is further submitted that the alleged transaction relates to the year 2016, therefore, no court shall take cognizance after lapse of three years of transaction, which is clearly barred under Section 468 Cr.P.C.
In view of the above, the matter requires consideration.
Issue notice to opposite party no. 2.
Steps to be taken within a week.
List in the week commencing 20.02.2023.
In the meantime, no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicant."
Thereafter, the applicant No.1 alongwith his other family members have been implicated in the present case for the same cause of action, which is nothing but an abuse of process of law.

Shri S.P. Tiwari, learned A.G.A. for the State-opposite party No.1 made a preliminary objection regarding the contentions made by learned Counsel for the applicants and submits that the applicants have an alternate remedy to approach the concerned Magistrate under Section 210 Cr.P.C. for redressal of their grievances.

Section 210 of the Criminal Procedural Code, 1973 is reproduced hereinunder:-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Procedure to be followed when there is a complaint case and police investigation in respect of the same offence.

(1) When in a case instituted otherwise than on a police report (hereinafter referred to as a complaint case), it is made to appear to the Magistrate, during the course of the inquiry or trial held by him, that an investigation by the police is in progress in relation to the offence which is the subject-matter of the inquiry or trial held by him,
the Magistrate shall stay the proceedings of such enquiry or trial and call for a report on the matter from the police officer conducting the investigation.

(2) If a report is made by the investigating police officer under section 173 and on such report cognizance of any offence is taken by the Magistrate against any person who is an accused in the complaint case, the Magistrate shall inquire into or try together the complaint case and the case arising out of the police report as if both the cases were instituted on a police report.

(3) If the police report does not relate to any accused in the complaint case or if the Magistrate does not take cognizance of any offence on the police report, he shall proceed with the inquiry or trial, which was stayed by him, in accordance with the provisions of this Code."

After considering the submissions made by learned Counsel for the parties and after perusal of record, this Court is of the view that the applicant may approach the concerned Magistrate under Section 210 Cr.P.C. by filing an appropriate application within 15 days' from today and if any such,
application is moved by the applicants, the concerned Magistrate is directed to decide the same within two months from the date of filing of such application.
Till the period of two months from the date of filing of such application or till disposal of the aforesaid application, whichever is earlier no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in pursuance of the aforesaid case.
With the aforesaid observations/directions, the present application is hereby disposed of.
